title: Restore the homepage
briefing: Ticket: the website's homepage is blank.
Someone renamed the real index.html to index.html.bak while 'fixing' it,
and left a junk index.html.tmp behind. Put it right.
expert_objective: Restore ~/site: index.html.bak -> index.html, and remove index.html.tmp.
tips: This is just the tools you already have: `mv` to rename, `rm` to delete.
objective: In ~/site: rename index.html.bak back to index.html, and delete the leftover index.html.tmp.
hints: Two problems: the real page has the wrong name, and there's a junk file to remove. Fix both.
Rename the backup back: `mv index.html.bak index.html`. Then delete the tmp file with `rm`.
solution:
cd ~/site
mv index.html.bak index.html
rm index.html.tmp
explanation: Nothing new here — just `mv` and `rm` used together to fix a real-looking mess. That's most of system administration: small, careful moves with tools you already know. You finished Level 1: files bend to your will.
